title: Bind a review request to a work product and explicit Git range
mechanism: At the pinned Superpowers revision, the requester supplies a description, requirements and a base/head diff to a separate reviewer, then triages Critical, Important and Minor findings. The reviewer template asks for file-and-line findings that explain defect, impact and repair, followed by a reasoned merge assessment. The intended history isolation is a written workflow rule; these two documents do not implement process or context isolation. The caller's five-field list omits PLAN_REFERENCE, which is a sixth distinct literal used by the template. A caller integrating this template must resolve both plan fields and bind the Git range to the actual work being reviewed. The supplied HEAD~1 example compares committed trees and does not include uncommitted edits.
corrections: The extra template field is PLAN_REFERENCE; PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS already appears in both documents. Do not claim it is absent from the reviewer template.
Giving feedback only on reviewed code does not forbid reading unchanged callers, schemas or dependencies. A diff is the supplied entry point, not a stated read confinement boundary.
Treat history isolation, review cadence and severity handling as prescriptions, not as observed tool behavior or guaranteed defect prevention.
There is no explicit fix-to-rerun or issue-tracking protocol in these two units. Do not infer remediation closure from a requested fix or a merge verdict.
The documents' two template-path spellings are visible, but no deployed resolver failure was demonstrated. The example outputs are illustrations, not test or review results.
source_scope: The complete four admitted source files across this three-record packet were read at the pinned Git revision. Scope is prescriptive text interpretation; no native tool execution or efficacy test was performed.
adoption_boundary: Useful as a review-request and finding-format design reference. Apply the current project's scope, authorization and verification rules; this source does not authorize spawning agents, changing a repository, or imposing its per-task review cadence.
